articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026 Opening Ceremony Date, Start Time, TV Info and Live Stream
articles.summary: The 2026 Presidents Cup is set to tee off Thursday at Medinah Country Club Course No. 3 near Chicago, pitting some of the best golfers from the United States and around the world against each other in an international competition.
articles.body:
The 2026 Presidents Cup is set to tee off Thursday at Medinah Country Club Course No. 3 near Chicago, pitting some of the best golfers from the United States and around the world against each other in an international competition.

The Golf Channel will be providing live coverage for the first two days of the event before NBC and Peacock take over on Saturday and Sunday.

Here's a breakdown of this weekend's schedule for the 2026 Presidents Cup.

Presidents Cup Opening Ceremony, Noon-12:30 p.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 1 Matches- Fourballs, 12:30-7 p.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 2 Matches- Foursomes, 2-7 p.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 3 Matches- Fourballs, 8-9 a.m. ET (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

Round 4 Matches- Fourballs and Foursomes, 9 a.m. ET-7 p.m. ET (NBC/Peacock)

Final Round Matches- Singles, Noon-6 p.m. ET (NBC/Peacock)

The Presidents Cup pits 12 U.S. golfers against 12 international players from everywhere in the world except Europe. The U.S. has won 10 straight showdowns, most recently earning an 18.5-11.5 victory at Royal Montreal Golf Club two years ago.

Brandt Snedeker is the captain of the U.S. team, while Australia's Geoff Ogilvy is the international team captain.

Fans will be excited to see if the U.S. can continue its dominance or if the international team finally breaks through this year.

articles.title: Aaron Rai and Tiger Woods’ unlikely full-circle story: From old VHS tapes to the PGA Championship winner meeting his childhood golfing hero
articles.summary: Explore the inspiring story of Aaron Rai, who became a PGA Championship winner influenced by his childhood hero, Tiger Woods. Discover how Rai's admiration for Woods shaped his golfing journey and led to his historic achievement.
articles.body: Aaron Rai’s road to major championship glory is linked to Tiger Woods’ influence. Woods was a major influence on Rai growing up long before he became a professional golfer, with Rai and his father Amrik often watching VHS tapes of the American star’s performances.That early fascination became part of Rai’s professional motivation. Years later, Rai met Woods in person, a moment that connected his childhood hero worship with his life as a professional golfer. Then came his win at the 2026 PGA Championship, and another big chapter was added to a story that began with those childhood viewings.Inside Aaron Rai and Tiger Woods’ unlikely full-circle story leading to the PGA ChampionshipAaron Rai was born and raised in Wolverhampton, England, in a family where golf was a big part of life. Amrik, his father, had a big role in developing his son's game, searching for information that could help Rai understand golf technique, particularly the mechanics of the swing.That process became a big part of Tiger Woods. Rai and his father would watch old VHS tapes of Woods, including footage of the American’s historic amateur career and major championship wins. The videos enabled young Rai to learn from one of the sport’s most impactful figures, as well as be inspired during his own development.Rai was studying Woods' three consecutive victories at the U.S. Amateur Championship from 1994 to 1996. Another fascination was the way he dominated the major championships in the early 2000s.To Rai, the recordings were more than entertainment. They were part of his education in the sport and helped shape his understanding of what was possible at the highest level.Tiger Woods connection shaped Aaron Rai’s golf journeyAs his own golf career developed, so did his admiration for Woods. The link took on a special significance in 2013 when Rai and his father went to Muirfield for The Open Championship to try and catch a glimpse of Woods during a practice round.The pair are said to have driven through the night and arrived early in the morning. At that stage Rai didn’t get the chance to meet Woods one-on-one, but the experience showed how big a part Woods played in his golfing journey.A decade later, Rai finally got to meet Woods at the pro-am for the 2023 Genesis Invitational. It was an opportunity for Rai to meet the player he had been following since childhood.Rai also walked the final nine holes of one of Woods’ practice rounds at that tournament. Watching Woods took time away from his own professional golfer preparation routine, highlighting the enduring significance of his childhood hero.The two golfers did not have formal mentorship. Woods’ influence was mainly from watching him, his career, his performances and his approach to the game.That distinction makes the story even more important. Rai created his own professional golfer’s persona, bringing with him lessons and inspiration from a player he had watched for years.Aaron Rai’s childhood inspiration leads to PGA ChampionshipRai’s biggest career achievement came as a breakout at the 2026 PGA Championship. He closed with a five-under 65 at Aronimink Golf Club to claim the Wanamaker Trophy.His final round was also part of an unusual scoring achievement. Rai improved his score in all four rounds, moving from 70 to 69, then 67 and finally 65.His consistency gave his victory a significant historical context. Rai’s victory was the first PGA Championship win for an Englishman since Jim Barnes in 1919 and ended a long wait for an English-born champion at the event.The victory also lent more significance to some of Rai's quirky golfing habits, many of which are tied to his upbringing and his relationship with his late father.Rai is known for wearing two gloves when he plays, rather than the single glove worn by professional golfers. The habit started in his childhood in England, when he would wear gloves on both hands to help him get through the cold conditions during practice.Aaron Rai’s historic win honors his family rootsAaron Rai is also still getting covers on his irons. It’s the same practice as his father’s approach to equipment and sacrifices made to get Rai quality clubs when he was young.Those habits have remained with Rai even as he’s risen to elite professional golfer status. They are a reminder of a previous time in his career, of the family support that helped build his foundation in the sport.MilestoneSignificanceChildhoodRai watched Tiger Woods footage with his father, Amrik1994–1996 footageWoods’ three U.S. Amateur victories became part of Rai’s viewing2013Rai and his father travelled to Muirfield to watch Woods2023Rai met Woods at the Genesis Invitational2026Rai won the PGA Championship at Aronimink Golf ClubRai’s PGA Championship win is thus not like any other standard breakthrough story. One can see several stages in his success, from being exposed to Woods as a child, to years of pro development, to a long-awaited meeting with his idol, and finally to winning a major championship of his own.The symbolism is even more powerful because Woods was the gold standard for the young Rai, and Rai has carved out his own place in the history of major championships.The link does not mean that Woods was the direct architect of Rai’s success. Instead, it shows how one athlete can shape the dreams of another, long before the two ever share the same professional space.From watching Woods on VHS tapes with his dad to meeting him as an established pro, Rai’s story already had a pretty incredible full-circle moment, and the defining achievement was winning the 2026 PGA Championship, turning that childhood inspiration into one of golf’s most memorable personal journeys.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns to partner for first Thursday fourballs match for Team USA
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns will take on Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im as the first group to go out on Thursday's fourballs at the Presidents Cup, as both captains revealed their pairings on Wednesday; watch Thursday's fourballs live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Brandt Snedeker's Team USA are looking to extend their winning streak to 11 consecutive victories over the International team at Medinah Country Club.

Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele head out in match two and will take on Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune.

Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele will head out in match two and will take on Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune.

Snedeker has chosen to pair experienced Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup player Justin Thomas alongside 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun for match three.

They'll take on Canadian Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria of Colombia.

A blockbuster group will go out in the fourth match of the day, with two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa taking on the reigning Open champion Ryan Fox and 2013 Masters winner Adam Scott.

Chris Gotterup will pair with Patrick Cantlay in the final game of the fourballs session against Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim.

Match one will get under way at 5.35pm (UK and Ireland time) with the International team set to take the honours off the tee.

Thursday fourballs and tee times (all UK and Ireland time)

Match 1 (1735): Scottie Scheffler/Sam Burns vs Min Woo Lee/Sungjae Im

Match 2 (1753): Cameron Young/Xander Schauffele vs Hideki Matsuyama/Ryo Hisatsune

Match 3 (1811): Justin Thomas/Jackson Koivun vs Corey Conners/Nico Echavarria

Match 4 (1829): Wyndham Clark/Collin Morikawa vs Ryan Fox/Adam Scott

Match 5 (1847): Chris Gotterup/Patrick Cantlay vs Tom Kim/Si Woo Kim

Scheffler, Burns out to end unwanted streak

Scheffler and Burns have struggled together in past team events, despite being good friends, with the duo having fallen to an underwhelming record of 0-3-1 at the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup.

"Do I think we have unfinished business? I don't know if I would call it that," Burns said.

"It's been frustrating the times we have played together, and we feel like we've played really well and ultimately not won," Burns said. "It's been more frustrating than anything.

"Yeah, this week we're going to go out and compete as hard as we can and try to get as many points for the US team as possible."

Snedeker also delved into his decision to pair up Koivun and Thomas, explaining the decision was an easy one given how well the two pair together.

"Jackson being a young kid, I feel like he's really kind of found his way on our team really quickly," Snedeker said on Wednesday. "I feel like he's handled the adjustment really well. Justin is just a natural pairing for him.

"He's somebody he's comfortable with. He'll do a great job putting his arm around him and show him how USA golf is meant to be played.

"I think we're really excited about all these match-ups and put this line-up out."

Fox taking inspiration from Europe's Ryder Cup stars

Open champion Fox is hoping the International Team can channel the energy of Team Europe at the 2025 Ryder Cup and are motivated to win for Scott.

"For us, we've always been the underdogs in this," Fox said.

"But I feel like on paper the European Ryder Cup team is always the underdogs a little bit, and that hasn't seemed to affect their results at all over the last few years.

"We're trying to channel a little bit of that and come together.

"We do have a chance to do something incredible when we've got a couple of guys on the team who have played a lot of these that we really want to get a win for. That's our motivation. I mean, Adam [Scott] especially over there.

"We're trying to flip the pressure on the US. I feel like they're expected to win, and if we can get on top early and create some pressure, there will be more pressure come on them from other places and hopefully we can take advantage of that."

articles.title: US seeks 11th Presidents Cup win in a row over global foes
articles.summary: United States golfers will try to stretch their win streak to 11 while the Internationals seek their first victory since 1988 when the 16th Presidents Cup be...
articles.body:
United States golfers will try to stretch their win streak to 11 while the Internationals seek their first victory since 1988 when the 16th Presidents Cup begins Thursday at Medinah.

The Americans own a 13-1-1 edge over their non-European global rivals in a biennial series that has failed to produce the drama and tension of the US-Europe Ryder Cup rivalry.

The Internationals' lone triumph came 28 years ago at Australia's Royal Melbourne with a 2003 draw in South Africa their only other bright spot.

The global squad will try to pull off a "Miracle at Medinah" in the footsteps of Europe's 2012 Ryder Cup fightback from 10-6 down with eight wins and a draw in singles for a 14.5-13.5 victory at the suburban Chicago layout.

But they will not be drawing much inspiration from that comeback.

"We really just focus on what we're doing," said Internationals captain Geoff Ogilvy of Australia. "The boys are excited. We all have memories, pretty vivid memories, of watching that Sunday at that Ryder Cup, just as an interested observer.

"We take our own inspirations from our own sort of stuff."

US captain Brandt Snedeker, who won his 10th PGA Tour title in May at Myrtle Beach, had no clue why the Americans could dominate the Presidents Cup yet lose nine of the past 12 Ryder Cups.

"Trying to figure out the secret sauce, if you will, of why the success has been this way is the hardest question we're trying to answer," Snedeker said.

"The makeup of every team is different. The bonding in every team is different. So trying to navigate that is really difficult."

Americans boast eight of the top 11 players in the world rankings with world number one Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Collin Morikawa and Russell Henley plus captain's picks Chris Gotterup and Xander Schauffele.

Other US captain's picks include Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay and rookies Jacob Bridgeman, a winner last week at Biltmore, and Jackson Koivun, a 21-year-old who won the 3M Open in July in only his third professional start.

Scheffler is only 3-5-1 in prior Presidents Cup appearances but Snedeker is not worried about the reigning PGA FedEx Cup champion.

"Scottie Scheffler being Scottie Scheffler is the most important thing for us as a team. We can't ask him to do more than he can do," Snedeker said.

"He can only deliver five points at his best, if he goes out and plays unbelievable. We just want Scottie to go out there, be comfortable, have fun and be the Scottie Scheffler he is every week.

"I don't want him to take a burden on. He's not going to win or lose us this Presidents Cup. The Presidents Cup is won or lost by 12 people."

Ogilvy, the 2006 US Open champion, helped in a redesign of Medinah, which reopened in 2024 and could play soft this week due to rain.

"From an architecture standpoint, I would love to see it play firm. We built it to play firm," he said.

"To see some things played out exactly as we thought, and then other things it has... just been fun to watch them play it."

South Korean Kim Si-woo is the top-ranked Internationals golfer at 13th followed by New Zealand rookie Ryan Fox at 24th.

Other veterans include Japan's Hideki Matsuyama, South Korean Tom Kim and Australians Min Woo Lee and Adam Scott, who makes his 12th Presidents Cup start still seeking his first victory.

Ogilvy's captain's choices included three rookies -- Japan's Ryo Hisatsune, Canada's Nick Taylor and Colombian Nico Echavarria -- plus Canada's Corey Conners, South Korean Im Sung-jae and South African Christiaan Bezuidenhout.

"The spirit of this group is really strong. I think we're more together than we've ever been," Ogilvy said. "I think the time is right. The boys know we're close. They want to win this."

articles.title: Rams news: Davante Adams won't rule out Packers troll job during upcoming game
articles.summary: On Monday evening, the Los Angeles Rams got into the win column for the first time this season with a blowout home victory over the New York Giants in primet...
articles.body:
On Monday evening, the Los Angeles Rams got into the win column for the first time this season with a blowout home victory over the New York Giants in primetime. The star of this game for Los Angeles was wide receiver Davante Adams , who hauled in eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns in the victory.

The Rams have several marquee games coming up on the schedule this year, including a matchup against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. Recently, Adams spoke on what he might have in store for that matchup against his former team , including a potential Lambeau Leap at SoFi Stadium.

"You can't really. You can a little bit because there's little suites behind (the field), kind of like there was at Allegiant… The Lambeau wall is up there. You've got to really jump to get up there… We'll see what we can do," he said, per Up & Adams on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Adams sure looked like the Packers All-Pro version of himself on Monday against New York, consistently finding seams in the Giants' secondary, helped by the fact that reigning MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford had a bounce-back game after his season-opening dud against the San Francisco 49ers last week.

Overall, the Rams looked much more like the team many expect them to be this year in this game, despite playing without superstar Myles Garrett , who is on the IR with a knee injury following his ugly debut against the 49ers.

In any case, the Rams will look to get over .500 for the first time this season when they next hit the field on Sunday evening for a tough road game against the Denver Broncos at 8:20 pm ET.

articles.title: Jets news: David Bailey injury is nothing to worry about, but other update is bad
articles.summary: The New York Jets recently suffered their first loss of the season with a tough overtime defeat at the hands of the Green Bay Packers at home. Making matters...
articles.body:
The New York Jets recently suffered their first loss of the season with a tough overtime defeat at the hands of the Green Bay Packers at home. Making matters worse was the fact that defensive end David Bailey appeared to suffer an injury during the contest, causing some fans to wonder about his status moving forward.

Thankfully, on Wednesday, the team got a positive update on that front.

"David Bailey has an elbow injury but Glenn said he's fine," reported Brian Costello of the New York Post on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

However, it wasn't all good news on the injury front for the Jets on Wednesday.

"DT David Onyemata had core-muscle surgery. Expected to be back by the end of the year, per Glenn," reported Rich Cimini of ESPN on X.

It's unclear exactly how long Onyemata's recovery process is expected to take, but clearly, he isn't anticipated to be back anytime soon.

In his absence, it will be up to Bailey and the other members of the Jets' restructured defensive line, which lost Quinnen Williams via trade last season, to pick up the slack.

Overall, the Jets have been more competitive than many expected so far this year, knocking off the Tennessee Titans in blowout fashion in Week 1 on the road before giving the Packers all they could handle on Sunday afternoon.

Thus far, Aaron Glenn seems to have the team playing inspired football, even as his clock management woes of last year have clearly not improved in 2026.

In any case, the Jets will next hit the field on Sunday for a tough road game vs the Detroit Lions . Kickoff is set for 1:00 pm ET.

articles.title: Tramon Williams’ pick-6 among great Packers performances against Falcons
articles.summary: You never pass up an excuse to talk about Tramon Williams burning Atlanta.
articles.body:
The Packers and Falcons will meet for the 37th time in the regular season tomorrow night. While not exactly a storied rivalry, these two teams have certainly had a few interesting matchups, and they've produced a few great performances for the Packers as well.

Here are the highlights, including one game from all the way back in 1970.

Passing yards – 396 ( Aaron Rodgers, 2011 )

En route to his first MVP, Aaron Rodgers sliced and diced the Atlanta Falcons ' secondary in 2011, following up his one-man destruction of the Georgia Dome in the playoffs the previous year. His 396 yards included 140 just to James Jones , who went 70 yards for a touchdown in the third quarter to give the Packers' the lead for the first time in what would become a 25-14 win.

Rushing yards – 155 ( Ahman Green, 2002 )

In some grim foreshadowing, the Packers had trouble with Michael Vick at Lambeau Field to open up the 2002 season . The Falcons, however, had even more trouble with Ahman Green, who carried 27 times for 155 yards to help the Packers to a 37-34 overtime victory. Green also added 42 yards on six catches.

Samkon Gado gets an honorable mention here, too. He rushed for 103 yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta in 2005 , but we'll have more from him later on.

A second honorable mention goes to Donny Anderson, the only player in Packers history to surpass the 100-yard mark against the Falcons twice: once in 1968 and once in 1969 .

Receiving yards – 186 ( Carroll Dale, 1970 )

I'd have guessed the top yardage game would have come from either James Jones in the aforementioned 2011 game or from Jordy Nelson circa 2014, but Carroll Dale had both of them beat before Jones or Nelson was even born.

In 1970, Dale caught four passes for 186 yards and two touchdowns, including an 89-yard strike from Don Horn that put the Packers ahead for good. Horn's pass traveled an impressive 56 yards in the air, which would have been the longest completion by air yards in the NFL in 2025.

I told you we'd mention Samkon Gado again. Well, here we are.

Dr. Gado is one of two Packers to score three touchdowns in a game against the Falcons, doing so in the aforementioned 2005 game. In that game, he rushed for two touchdowns and added a third through the air to cap off a four catch, five yard, one touchdown receiving performance.

The other Packers player to hit a touchdown triumvirate against the Falcons is Robert Tonyan . Big Bob put three across against the Falcons in 2020 as a part of a dominant Packers win .

Squaring off against the Falcons at Milwaukee County Stadium, the Packers got a serious boost from Tim Harris via his four sacks. One came on the Falcons' final drive , which helped preserve the Packers' 23-21 victory.

Also noteworthy, Za'Darius Smith recorded three sacks against the Falcons in the Packers' 2020 win at Lambeau Field. Now a member of the Falcons, you have to think Smith has a pretty good shot at hitting that number again, especially if he's working against Anthony Belton .

A week after firing Mike McCarthy, the Packers got their first of two wins in the short-lived Joe Philbin era with a 34-20 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Blake Martinez led the defensive effort, recording 11 solo tackles as the Packers shut down the Falcons.

Counting playoff games, three different players have recorded two interceptions in a game against the Falcons.

Herb Adderley did it first, picking off the Falcons twice in 1968 .

Mark Murphy (no, not that one) did it next, also grabbing two interceptions during a 1988 shutout loss in Atlanta.

And finally, Tramon Williams did it best. His leaping interception late in the second quarter of the Packers' 2010 Divisional Round victory over the Falcons set up what would become the go-ahead drive for the Packers. The Packers scored so quickly that they left time on the clock for the Falcons to try to rally. They tried…and they got burned .

articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026: Latest scores, results, tee times, leaderboard as Team USA host International Team at Medinah
articles.summary: Team USA host the International Team at the Presidents Cup and chase an 11th consecutive victory; latest schedule and results from the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The four-day competition sees five sessions of golf played and a total of 30 points up for grabs, with five fourballs matches played on Thursday before five foursomes matches on Friday.

Four matches of both sessions are played on Saturday before all 24 players then tee it up in the Sunday singles, with the first team to reach 15.5 points across the week earning Presidents Cup victory.

Team USA, the defending champions and chasing an 11th consecutive win in the biennial contest, require 15 points to retain the trophy. The International Team are searching for just their second win and first since 1998, with Team USA winning 13 of the previous 15 editions.

Sky Sports will have live coverage from every session, with coverage getting under way at 5.30pm for Thursday's fourballs ahead of the first tee shot at 5.35pm (11.35am local time).

The afternoon foursomes are then live on Saturday from 7pm, with full coverage of the Sunday singles starting at 5pm on Sky Sports Golf and running until long after a winner has been crowned.

articles.title: Packers Legendary QB Lynn Dickey Blasts Coach Matt LaFleur
articles.summary: Lynn Dickey, who's in the Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame, ripped coach Matt LaFleur for the team's l;ack of discipline.
articles.body:
Quarterback Lynn Dickey is a Green Bay Packers legend.

And Wednesday Dickey went on a legendary rant, calling out Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur.

Appearing on The Bill Michaels Show, Dickey lambasted LaFleur and the Packers for their ridiculous 26 penalties through two games. Not only does Green Bay lead the league in penalties and penalty yards (231), the Packers are on pace to set NFL records in both of those categories.

Green Bay is 1-1 heading into its game with Atlanta Thursday night, and LaFleur has become the frontrunner to be the first coach fired this season.

"I don't know the personality of Matt LaFleur, but it sure appears to be very passive, and like, 'I don't want to get down guys' throats.' But sometimes that's what you've got to do," Dickey said of the Packers' penalty issues. "They make a lot of money. We all know that. But you've got to want to be disciplined and controlled and the way this thing is going right now, boy does it stink. I'd like to say something different about it, but that's what I see."

Dickey, who quarterbacked the Packers from 1976-85, threw for 21,369 yards and 133 touchdowns in that time. In 1983, Dickey powered the Packers to a then-team record 429 points and threw a league-high 32 touchdown passes.

Dickey still ranks second in team history for most passing yards in a season (4,458 in 1983). He also holds the Green Bay record for highest completion percentage in a game with a minimum of 20 attempts (19–21, 90.48%) against New Orleans in 1981.

Dickey played for Bart Starr from 1976-1983, then under Forrest Gregg his final two seasons in Green Bay. While the Packers lacked discipline under Gregg, they were consistently among the NFL's least penalized teams with Starr in charge.

"We didn't have the greatest talent when I played, but almost every year we were in the top-three of fewest penalties," said Dickey, who's a member of the Packers' Hall of Fame. "And why?

"Bart Starr went over and over and over and demanded that all the time. And I see the stupid penalties post-play, unsportsmanlike stuff. You know, that's all coaching. And just right now man, it is a bomb. And something better change."

At this point, Dickey certainly isn't optimistic that will happen.

"(They're) the most undisciplined team," Dickey said during the radio show. "Penalties are coaching and if you don't get after people and demand that they do the correct things, that's coaching."

articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026: How to watch the U.S. and International squads at Medinah
articles.summary: The Presidents Cup tees off on Sept. 24 as the United States and the International squads go head-to-head at Medinah Country Club in the biennial competition...
articles.body:
The Presidents Cup begins Thursday, Sept. 24, when the United States and the International squads go head-to-head at Medinah Country Club Course No. 3.

U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker leads the Stars and Stripes as they take on Geoff Ogilvy's roster that boasts a trio of major winners in Adam Scott, Hideki Matsuyama and Ryan Fox.

The U.S. leads the one-sided, biennial affair , 13-1-1. The lone International Team victory came in 1998 in Australia.

Golf Channel and Golf Channel mobile will provide live, on-site coverage all week from Medinah to keep fans in the know on everything happening inside and outside of the ropes.

During Wednesday's live show, Snedeker and Ogilvy will reveal their pairings for the first fourball matches. That is scheduled to take place at 4:45 p.m. ET.

Here's a look at how you can stay locked in all of the news and action from the 16th edition of the Presidents Cup :

Noon-12:30PM: Presidents Cup, Opening Ceremony (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

12:30-7PM: Presidents Cup, Day 1 fourballs (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

7-9PM: Live From the Presidents Cup (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

2-7PM: Presidents Cup, Day 2 foursomes (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

8-9AM: Presidents Cup, Day 3 fourballs (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

9AM-7PM: Presidents Cup, Day 3 fourballs and foursomes (NBC/Peacock)

Noon-6PM: Presidents Cup, final-day singles (NBC/Peacock)

6-8PM: Live From the Presidents Cup (Golf Channel/GC mobile)

The first session features five fourball matches, the first of which tees off at 12:35 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kansas State Football: Depth Chart Review vs Tulane- Defense
articles.summary: After a slow start, the Wildcat defense took control, but questions about the run defense linger.
articles.body:
Wendell Gregory : Snaps – 50 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 3 – Sacks – .5

Darien Whitaker Jr. : Snaps – 43 – Tackles – 3 – T.F.L. – 1.5 – Sacks – 1.5

Jayden Bryant: Snaps – 29 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 2 – Sacks – 2

Elijah Hill : Snaps – 11 – Tackles – 1 – T.F.L. – 1 – Sacks – 1

I split the defensive ends and interior defensive linemen because one group dominated the game while the other struggled. The Defensive ends contributed 7.5 tackles for loss and 5 sacks. That's domination. Gregory and Whitaker look like an elite defensive end pairing, with Bryant and Hill providing quality depth. The Wildcats are 3rd in the nation in tackles for loss. I'm pretty sure they're around the top in sacks as well, but the NCAA's stats website is refusing to give up the data.

Gregory and Whitaker Jr. are the clear headliners, but don't sleep on Jayden Bryant. He brought some extra juice to the pass rush as well. Tulane struggled to find him when he was on the field.

This group is playing like one of the nation's best defensive end groups and, in fact, might be one of the best defensive end groups in the nation.

Kamari Burns: Snaps – 34 – Tackles – 2 – T.F.L. – .5

If you're looking for something to worry about, I've got you. The interior defensive line struggled mightily in this one. Travis Bates looked like a defensive end playing defensive tackle while struggling to get off blocks in the run game. PFF credited him with 2 QB hurries, which is great for a defensive tackle, but he also missed 2 tackles, which isn't so great. 52 snaps with no recordable stats isn't a great outing.

Kamari Burns wasn't much better. He was credited with 2 stops, but like Bates, he also had 2 missed tackles. Burns did a better job of holding his ground, but Tulane was able to find some space in the A and B gaps. Eli Jackson did some good things in his 21 snaps, but man, Burns has to stay healthy because a Jackson and Bates pairing would be an open invitation to run inside.

If I were an opposing offensive coordinator, my entire focus would be finding ways to exploit K-State's undersized and thin (in terms of depth) interior line. Tulane's offensive line got some real push up the middle, and their backs were able to hit holes at full speed, making tackling at the second level difficult for the linebackers and safeties.

The coaching staff will have to work around this issue all season. They really need another run-stuffing defensive tackle to emerge. The Wildcats may be the only P4 team in the nation where 2 of the top 3 defensive tackles on the roster are significantly under 300 pounds.

Gabe Powers: Snaps – 61 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 1.5 – Sacks – 0 – Force Fumbles – 1

Mekhi Mason: Snaps – 43 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 1 – Sacks – 1

Rex Van Wyhe: Snaps – 22 – Tackles – 5 – T.F.L. – 1 – Sacks – 0

Speaking of undersized, Mason and Powers are fine individually, but as a pair, they play better running sideline to sideline than getting downhill and taking on running backs in the hole. Ideally, one of them would carry a little more weight in their rear end to hold up against a power running attack. Powers got dinged for 2 missed tackles, and while Mason didn't miss any tackles, it felt like he wasn't in position to make as many as he should have in the run game.

Thankfully, Rex Van Wyhe has emerged as a functional running-stuffing option at linebacker. He made the most of his 22 snaps and, at 245 pounds, is better suited to take on offensive linemen head-on. Van Wyhe played the best game of his Kansas State career against Tulane and could see more action moving forward, especially against run-oriented teams.

Depth is also a major concern at this spot.

Kaleb Patterson: Snaps – 62 – Tackles – 2 – Pass Break-Ups – 1

JoJo Scott: Snaps – 55 – Tackles – 2 – Pass Break-Ups – 1

Rich was targeted 3 times and gave up 3 receptions. That seems bad until you realize those 3 receptions totaled 20 yards, with a long of 12. Tulane decided not to challenge CB1, which was a smart decision.

Since the ball wasn't heading Zashon's way, Kaleb Patterson and JoJo Scott saw plenty of action. Patterson was targeted 5 times and gave up 2 receptions. Unfortunately, those two receptions totaled 41 yards. JoJo Scott was targeted 6 times and gave up 2 receptions. Unfortunately, those two receptions totaled 52 yards, including a 41-yarder.

The thing about playing with a legit lockdown corner like Rich is that the ball tends to head your way more often than usual. Patterson and Scott are going to be tested by every team on Kansas State's schedule. Rich, Patterson, and Scott pretty much went the distance on Saturday. Tulane's offense didn't require more than 3 corners on the field.

The coaching staff brought in Ben Osueke, who started 12 games for Temple last season and was on the All-AAC 3rd team in 2025, last week. I'll be interested to see if he makes it onto the field against Cincinnati.

Wesley Fair: Snaps – 51 – Tackles – 8 – T.F.L. – .5

Logan Bartley : Snaps – 16 – Tackles – 3

Beasley is an interesting case. He was a 4-star, top-150 recruit and was considered the 6th-best player in Ohio coming out of high school. He signed with Ryan Walters and Purdue , witnessed the football equivalent of the Hindenburg as a freshman, and hit the eject button. After a year of football rehab at Miami, Ohio, he's starting for Kansas State. This dude was one of the fastest players in the class of 2024, and he sort of fell into Kansas State's lap, almost as an afterthought. Now you're starting to see what all of the recruiting fuss was about. His speed is a difference-maker in the back end. He can outrun 99% of receivers. Seriously, no one is throwing the ball over his head. He's not very big and is going to miss some tackles in run support (he missed 2 against Tulane), but that's why guys like Logan Bartley are on the roster. To steal from the running backs, Beasley is the lighting and Bartley is the thunder.

Unfortunately, the thunder went down with an injury early, but most teams can't bring their 2025 starter off the bench if their 2026 starter gets hurt. Fair's 8 tackles led the Wildcats, and he was also credited with a team-high 3 "stops" by PFF, while only missing one tackle. Tulane targeted him once in the passing game and completed a 6-yard pass. I thought Bartley going down was going to be a big blow to the defense, but Fair stepped in and didn't miss a beat.

Beasley kept a lid on the defense from his free safety position, and Fair terrorized the Green Wave around the line of scrimmage. After last season, the safety position felt all but safe, but it may be one of the deepest and most talented position groups on the roster with the addition of Beasley, the emergence of Bartley, and the dependability of Fair. That's not even taking into consideration All-ACC honorable mention safety Ja'son Prevard and Georgia transfer Adrian Maddox, who at one point were considered potential starters for the Wildcats.

It's truly an embarrassment of riches on the back end of the defense.

articles.title: Mets' Nolan McLean puts finishing touches on excellent rookie campaign: 'Proud of him'
articles.summary: Mets right-hander Nolan McLean ended his rookie campaign by going 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA, eighth-lowest in the NL, in 31 starts.
articles.body:
Before Wednesday's game between the Mets and Texas Rangers , manager Andy Green was asked what is the biggest area in Nolan McLean 's game that he can take a step forward in to reach that next level that the skipper always talks about.

Green mentioned the right-hander throwing strikes consistently and limiting his walks, but was quick to say, "and that's not by diminishing stuff, it's by using the stuff you have and understanding how to get ahead and to finish."

It was one of the many times this season that Green spoke about his young players in a way that seemed to challenge them – even when they've played great – because he knows they're capable of more.

Shortly thereafter, McLean took the mound and, heeding his manager's advice, looked amazing through four perfect innings. Things went awry for the rookie in the fifth inning, however, when the Rangers tagged him for two runs after McLean allowed three hits and a walk in the inning.

Just a few hours before that, Green practically predicted it.

"I actually think he does that really well for a pretty good portion of each game and then there's usually one inning where it's like here for a little, kinda lost it, now I found it again, now I compete, now I get out of it," the skipper said. "The less and less he does that, and look he's not gonna be perfect, but the more he drives that down and the less and less he does that he's gonna get himself out of more jams by not getting into them."

The foreshadowing by Green was uncanny, though it shouldn't come as a surprise considering he's known most of these young players since they joined the organization as the Senior Vice President for Player Development.

After that difficult fifth inning, McLean went right back to being dominant and retired the next six batters in order on just 13 pitches to complete his final outing of the season. Even in the fifth inning, the right-hander had the bases loaded with one out and managed to exit with just one run scoring.

"Those guys were aggressive so any time a team's aggressive like that and you're filling up the strike zone, you're relying a lot on your defense and sometimes they just don't hit it at guys and in the fifth inning they hit a few balls away from people and that's part of it," McLean said. "So I was just kind of trusting my stuff that they were eventually gonna hit it at people to try to minimize and if I get to two strikes I'll execute a pitch and punch him out.

"And then going back out in the sixth, making sure to keep that same game plan and not necessarily getting tentative just because they put a few balls in play [earlier]."

McLean ended his rookie campaign by going 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA, eighth-lowest in the NL, in 31 starts. He's also the only Mets starter this season who didn't miss a single start, impressive for a 25-year-old rookie whose season started at the World Baseball Classic pitching for Team USA.

"I try to take pride in going out there and competing every single time, whether I have my stuff or not and that's what matters most to me, just going out there and making each start," McLean said.

Meanwhile, Green, for all his challenges that he gives his players, was impressed with McLean's body of work and knows the right-hander will get back to work soon enough after he enjoys this one just a little while longer.

"I don't think that was like his vintage stuff and it still found a way to be really, really good," Green said about McLean's outing on Wednesday. "Velocity was a little bit down today. Last outing of a long season that started at the WBC and felt that he competed incredibly well today.

"He's just kind of the person he's been, just figure out a way to get it done even if it doesn't feel your best. So [I'm] proud of him, proud of the season he's had. He's got a lot to hang his hat on right now and I know it won't take long for him to get back to work and get going."

As for whether or not McLean did enough to take home the NL Rookie of the Year honors in what has become a solid class that includes teammate Carson Benge , Green isn't so sure his right-hander will be in the conversation.

Nevertheless, it doesn't take hardware to know what kind of pitcher McLean is.

"He's the best rookie pitcher in the National League and I think that's pretty obvious to everybody," Green said.

articles.title: Celtics news: Jayson Tatum, Paul George link up for golf outing
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum is getting one last break from the NBA grind before Boston Celtics training camp begins, and he spent it with some of his former teammates. Tat...
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum is getting one last break from the NBA grind before Boston Celtics training camp begins, and he spent it with some of his former teammates .

Tatum was recently spotted playing golf with Paul George and former Celtics teammate Malcolm Brogdon . Photos and videos from the outing made the rounds on social media, showing the three NBA veterans enjoying some downtime before the start of the 2026-27 season.

Celtics' social media account shared the image on X, formerly Twitter

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Squad goes golfing ⛳️," the caption read.

The group brought together former and current players from two Eastern Conference rivals, but there was plenty of history between them. Brogdon spent the 2022-23 season in Boston and won the Sixth Man of the Year award during his lone season with the Celtics. He later moved around the league before joining Philadelphia .

George, meanwhile, has remained one of Tatum's longtime friends . The two have worked out together during past offseasons and have often shown mutual respect for each other's games.

Their friendship has continued despite playing for teams that could see plenty of each other during the regular season. The offseason has also changed the connection between the Celtics and 76ers . Philadelphia added former Boston star Jaylen Brown as part of its roster overhaul.

For Tatum, the golf outing comes after a busy summer for Boston. The Celtics have gone through significant roster changes, leaving Tatum as the team's clear centerpiece heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

Training camp is now close, which means the relaxed days of the offseason are almost over.
